events.hidden_link: DIBAL-H reduces the nitrile to an aldehyde (Q). Acetal formation protects the aldehyde to give R. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis on the primary bromide yields exclusively a primary amine (S). Treatment with dry Ag₂O forms a symmetrical ether (T) rather than an alcohol.
events.route:
1. P to Q: DIBAL-H stops at the imine, which hydrolyzes to an aldehyde. Q has an aldehyde and an alkyl bromide.
2. Q to R: Methanol and dry HCl convert the aldehyde into a dimethyl acetal, protecting it, leaving the bromide intact.
3. R to S: Gabriel synthesis (phthalimide) selectively gives the primary amine. No overalkylation occurs.
4. R to T: Dry Ag₂O promotes the coupling of two alkyl halides into an ether, doubling the molecular formula. Moist Ag₂O would yield an alcohol.
events.student_must_notice: Gabriel synthesis yields exclusively a primary amine (S), giving a positive carbylamine test. Dry Ag₂O yields a symmetrical ether (T) instead of an alcohol, doubling the degree of unsaturation and number of carbons.
events.trap: Students might assume Gabriel synthesis can overalkylate to a secondary amine (failing the carbylamine test), or mistake dry Ag₂O for moist Ag₂O, yielding an alcohol (T) with half the actual degree of unsaturation.
